checks.name: runtime_match
checks.claim: The committed record is the runtime occurrence's: the instrumented engine served the control's tokens, every attempted value acquisition was bound, the committed bytes open against the run root, and no committed value differs from the Match oracle where the oracle looked.
notes: structural_leak: oracle_compare.NO_ORACLE_FAMILY_PREFIXES (kernel-interior streams excluded from the oracle by name prefix)

checks.name: local_replay
checks.claim: A post-commitment sample of required values replays exactly from the committed bytes under the Program's relations (C2 form (A)), over the required-value manifest Q(P) of record, with every unevaluated stratum named.
notes: structural_leak: sampled_replay.EVALUATORS / NOT_YET (which families the replay can evaluate is a table by family name (the stated applicability domain))

checks.name: boundary_linkage
checks.claim: Every (engine step, request) boundary is linked: the declared prompt to the input ids at the arrival step, and each sampled id to the next step's input id (C2 ordered boundary linkage).

checks.name: checkpoint_binding
checks.claim: Every served parameter the Program names equals, by digest, the checkpoint-composed tensor of record (MAN-09), with the shards pinned by their manifest sha256.
notes: structural_leak: weights_of_record.FUSED / EXPERTS / EXPERTS_MIXTRAL (the checkpoint composition of fused / expert tensors is keyed by known parameter-name tables)

checks.name: execution_extent
checks.claim: Each request's executed prefix of record (served length; the cap on a length stop, served + LAG on an EOS stop) is derived from the declared stop rule, linked to the Match account of the same attempt, and no committed row lies past it.

checks.name: required_value_coverage
checks.claim: Every identity of the required-value manifest Q(P) has exactly one committed binding, every required value class was acquired, and the manifest used is the one rebuilt from this attempt's Program x workload.
notes: structural_leak: required_manifest.members_for (a Program family is INTERIOR because the vocabulary names no member for it -- by name, F-r19-int-20)

checks.name: program_source_identity
checks.claim: The committed identities are the Program of record's: every step's committed identity set matches the expected manifest (X-03: modules, one attention row per layer, one sampled-ids tensor, the same multiset every step) and the binding map was built for this Program, layout and run roots.
notes: structural_leak: native_host.ACQUIRE_CLASSES (the expected module set is selected by module class name, not by the Program)
